Currently halfway into Stephen Baxter's "Raft", a book I've put off for way too long although I'm a big fan of the Xeelee Sequence. After a slow start I came to enjoy it quite a bit, even if it's pretty obviously an early piece of work. Characterisation and plot are rather mediocre, but at least the setting is quite interesting. Hoping there will be more about the universe and how the people got stuck there.

Last novel I finished was Charles Sheffield's "Tomorrow and Tomorrow", which I picked up because I'm a fan of deep time stories. It's a competent yarn that I'd recommend to people of similar interests, although I have my doubts about the motivations of the protagonist (who's really prepared to sit out such a humongous amount of time trying to be with your lover again? Or at least this particular protagonist.) Also I'm not completely sold on the future societies that are described. There's a good deal of originality in the alien worlds and their fauna, though.

I went through a weird streak recently. The last SF book that I really really enjoyed was Anathem. Lots of ideas to chew on and all my favorite speculative imagery. Since then I've also read The Moon is a Harsh Mistress (I burned through it but I did end up with a lot of questions), Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect (good and free in the vein of singularity thought experiment novellas), Blindsight (had some structure and writing issues but again the ideas were very interesting), Accelerando (or 100 pages of it; the thing is just one giant jargon nugget), and Sphere (Christ, this thing was a Big Mac of a book; you scarf down the whole thing and barely taste it). Now I'm reading 1491, which is anthropology about Pre-Columbian American Indian civilizations because I need a palette cleanser.
I'm digging into Roadside Picnic right now and plan to do a Jack McDevitt binge after this.
